overall: The AG found the Board violated the OML by late-approving open minutes, not reviewing executive session minutes, improperly using Purpose 6 on June 20, and posting an insufficient August 8 notice; no intentional violation was found.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to create and approve open session minutes from late 2022 and 2023 in a timely manner.
allegations.key_passage: In failing to timely approve 19 sets of minutes of open sessions, the Board violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to periodically review executive session minutes at reasonable intervals, with no review announced at any 2023 open session.
allegations.key_passage: As the Board did not review executive session minutes at regular intervals, it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly improperly invoked Purpose 6 for the June 20 executive session, which included state agency representatives and a discussion of a sign.
allegations.key_passage: Purpose 6 was defeated where representatives of state agencies also attended the executive session.

allegations.summary: Discussion of who would pay for a sign on town-owned property during the June 20 executive session did not concern purchase, exchange, lease or value of real property.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, it was improper to discuss the sign in executive session.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly improperly invoked Purpose 6 for the July 25 executive session on sale of the Spooner Street property.
allegations.key_passage: we are satisfied that it was appropriate for the Board to enter executive session under Purpose 6 on July 25 to discuss sale of the property on Spooner Street.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly improperly invoked Purpose 6 for lease and Holtec-related discussions at May through August 2023 executive sessions.
allegations.key_passage: Having reviewed the minutes of these executive sessions and having spoken with Town Counsel, we are satisfied that these discussions were proper under Purpose 6.

allegations.summary: The August 8 meeting notice listing 'Holtec (Value of Real Property)' allegedly was not sufficiently specific to inform the public.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, the notice description “Holtec (Value of Real Property)” fell short of the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged insufficient notices for meetings from May 16 through July 25, 2023, which was filed more than 30 days after those notices were discoverable.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the complaint is untimely as to allegations concerning the notices of those meetings.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the August 8 notice violation was intentional and that the Board showed a pattern or practice of violations.
allegations.key_passage: Nonetheless, we do not find an intentional violation in this instance.

remedy: Release the minutes of the August 8, 2023 executive session.
Release the portions of the June 20, 2023 executive session minutes that relate to subjects not appropriate for executive session under Purpose 6.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: Therefore, we order release of the minutes of the August 8 executive session and of the portions of the June 20 executive session which relate to those subjects that were not appropriate for executive session under Purpose 6. In addition, we order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
